passages.text: 1267. <sentence_start/>Efficacy and Safety of Switching to DTG/3TC in Virologically Suppressed PLWH by Age, Including Those Aged ≥65 Years: Pooled Results from the TANGO and SALSA Studies

The proportion of older adults living with HIV is growing, increasing the focus of managing age-related comorbidities and polypharmacy while maintaining virologic suppression. <sentence_start/>DTG/3TC is an international guidelines-recommended 2-drug regimen demonstrating high and durable efficacy, high barrier to resistance, and good safety and tolerability. <sentence_start/>We present pooled TANGO and SALSA efficacy and safety results analyzed by age (< 50, ≥ 50 to < 65, and ≥ 65 years).

Week 48 data from the open-label phase 3 TANGO and SALSA trials evaluating switch to once-daily DTG/3TC fixed-dose combination or continuing current antiretroviral regimen (CAR; TANGO: TAF-based; SALSA: NNRTI-/bPI-/INSTI-based) were pooled. <sentence_start/>Proportions of participants with HIV-1 RNA ≥ 50 and < 50 c/mL (Snapshot, ITT-E) and safety were analyzed by age.

Of 1234 participants (DTG/3TC, n=615; CAR, n=619), 71% were aged < 50 years, 26% aged 50 to < 65 years, and 3% aged ≥ 65 years. <sentence_start/>At Week 48, in participants aged 50 to < 65 years, 1 (< 1%) and 3 (2%) participants in the DTG/3TC and CAR groups, respectively, had HIV-1 RNA ≥ 50 c/mL, comparable to results in the overall population (Table 1). <sentence_start/>No participants aged ≥65 years had HIV-1 RNA ≥ 50 c/mL. <sentence_start/>Proportions with HIV-1 RNA < 50 c/mL were high regardless of age group. <sentence_start/>Adjusted mean change from baseline in CD4+ cell count and CD4+/CD8+ ratio was also consistent with overall results regardless of age (< 50 vs ≥ 50 years). <sentence_start/>No participants in the DTG/3TC group had confirmed virologic withdrawal (CVW); 1 participant in the CAR group had CVW (aged < 50 years; no resistance detected). <sentence_start/>Proportions of participants with baseline non-ART medication use and comorbidities increased with age in both treatment groups (Table 2). <sentence_start/>Across all age groups, proportions of any AEs were similar between the DTG/3TC and CAR groups, with few AEs leading to withdrawal and higher proportions of drug-related AEs with DTG/3TC vs CAR; similar results were observed in the overall population.

Among PLWH, switching to DTG/3TC maintained high rates of virologic suppression and demonstrated a favorable safety profile across all age groups, including those aged ≥65 years. <sentence_start/>As non-ART medication use and comorbidities increased with age, a well-tolerated 2-drug regimen may help older PLWH avoid drug interactions.
